sets.relationshipLabel: raw ingredient transformed into a new substance by a baking process
sets.explanation: Flour becomes dough and sugar becomes caramel — each pair is the same raw material remade into something structurally new through heat or hydration.

sets.relationshipLabel: the worker and the tool built for their trade
sets.explanation: A baker reaches for a peel just as a decorator reaches for a piping bag — each trade defined by the instrument it wields.

sets.relationshipLabel: the applied cover and the whole baked item it hides
sets.explanation: Fondant coats a wedding cake and marzipan coats a fruitcake — each cover is a layer applied over a whole finished item, not another piece of interior cake, so the covering-to-covered direction can't be reversed.

sets.relationshipLabel: the stage that opens a process and the stage that closes it
sets.explanation: Mixing starts the bake and cooling ends it, just as an apprentice begins a career that a master closes out — two spans framed by their first and last stage.
